edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 17

source_text: Idem sponsus dicitur et sponsa, pro locis et temporibus. Sicut sponso imposuit mihi mitram, et sicut sponsam ornavit me ornamento. Christus formam sui singulis accommodat causis: aliquando sponsus animae, aliquando sponsa Patris, aliquando sapientia quae quaeritur, aliquando Verbum quod quaerit. Liber I haec de osculo et uberibus et nomine et cellariis et aequitate digessit.
pass_a_gloss: Same bridegroom is-said and bride, for places and times. As to-bridegroom he-placed on-me mitre, and as bride he-adorned me with-ornament...
pass_b_english: The same one is called Bridegroom and Bride, according to places and times. [[As a bridegroom he has set a mitre on me, and as a bride he has adorned me with ornament >> Bible:Isaiah 61:10]]. Christ fits his form to each cause: sometimes Bridegroom of the soul, sometimes Bride of the Father, sometimes wisdom that is sought, sometimes Word that seeks. Book I has set out these things concerning the kiss and the breasts and the name and the chambers and equity.
